definition_en: a word used to give an affirmative answer or to show agreement
core_image: 下巴向下一顿，头点下去
scene: 老师问有没有人愿意帮忙，后排的男孩举手说愿意。 When the teacher asked for a volunteer, the boy at the back raised his hand and said yes.
sceneCN: 这里 yes 是「是、愿意」（第 1 个义项：表示肯定回答）；句意：老师问有没有人愿意帮忙时，后排的男孩举手说了愿意。

senses.title: An affirmative answer
senses.definition: used to answer a question in a positive way
senses.definitionCN: 用于对问题作出肯定的回答
senses.example: Are you ready? Yes, I am.
senses.exampleCN: 你准备好了吗？是的，我准备好了。
senses.why: The old form combines yea with so be it, so the core picture is a head nodding down on a decision.
senses.whyCN: 古形式是 yea 与「就这样吧」的结合，所以核心画面是头在决定上点下去。

senses.title: Agreement or permission
senses.definition: used to agree with a suggestion or to give permission
senses.definitionCN: 用于同意某个提议或给予许可
senses.example: Yes, you may borrow my bike.
senses.exampleCN: 可以，你可以借我的自行车。
senses.why: A nod that answers a question also grants a request, which supplies the permission sense.
senses.whyCN: 点头既回答了问题，也等于答应了请求，由此生出「许可、同意」的意思。

senses.title: A reply when called
senses.definition: used to answer when someone calls your name
senses.definitionCN: 别人叫你名字时用来应答
senses.example: Yes, coming in a moment.
senses.why: Answering a call is the smallest form of saying that one is present and agrees to come.
senses.whyCN: 回应一声呼唤，是「我在、我愿意来」最简短的表达。

senses.title: A positive vote or answer
senses.definition: a vote or answer in favour of something, countable as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 赞成某项提案的票或回答，可作可数名词
senses.example: The plan passed with fifty yeses.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划以五十张赞成票获得通过。
senses.why: The spoken word becomes a countable thing when votes are counted.
senses.whyCN: 当投票被点算时，说出口的那个词就变成可数的东西。

intro.en: Yes comes from Old English gese, a blend of gea, yea, and si, let it be so.
intro.cn: yes 来自古英语 gese，是 gea（是）与 si（就这样吧）的融合。

items.en: Gea means yes or indeed, and survives in the archaic English word yea.
items.cn: gea 意为「是、确实」，在古旧的英语词 yea 中留存下来。

items.en: Si means let it be so, and supplies the second half of gese.
items.cn: si 意为「就这样吧」，提供 gese 的后半部分。

items.en: Gese combines the two into a single emphatic yes.
items.cn: gese 把两者合成一个语气更强的「是」。

items.en: The form shortens to yes and replaces yea in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 中古英语中缩为 yes，并在日常口语中取代 yea。

items.en: Yes becomes a countable noun for a favourable vote or answer.
items.cn: 现代英语中 yes 成为可数名词，指赞成票或肯定回答。

note.en: Yes has several informal variants, and it stands opposite no in the vocabulary of answers.
note.cn: yes 有若干口语变体，并在回答用语中与 no 相对。

senses.title: Free from dirt
senses.definition: not dirty, with no marks or dust on it
senses.example: The kitchen is clean after washing.
senses.why: Clean goes back to Old English clǣne, 'clear, pure', and freedom from dirt is the word's centre.
senses.whyCN: clean 来自古英语 clǣne「洁净、纯粹」，不沾脏东西是它的核心。

senses.title: To remove dirt from something

senses.why: The adjective turned into a verb, so clean names the work of making something clean.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转作动词，clean 表示把某物弄干净这项工作。

senses.title: Complete and leaving nothing behind
senses.definition: complete, with nothing left out
senses.example: They made a clean sweep of the prizes.
senses.why: Something swept clean leaves no scrap behind on the floor, so clean also means 'complete, with nothing left'.
senses.whyCN: 扫得干干净净的地上不留一片碎屑，所以 clean 也表示「彻底、一点不剩」。

definition_en: a piece of furniture that people sleep on, or a flat base for something
core_image: 一张铺着厚被的木床，夜里把整天的疲惫都接住
scene: 夜深了，屋里的灯熄了，窗外的雨声盖过了脚步。 The child climbed into bed and fell asleep at once.
sceneCN: 这里 bed 是「睡觉的家具」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她早饭前整理了床铺。

collocations.zh: 提供住宿与早餐的旅店

derivatives.zh: 由 bed 加 -ing 构成，义为「床上用品」
由 bed 与 room 复合，义为「卧室」
由 bed 与 time 复合，义为「就寝时间」

senses.title: The furniture people sleep on
senses.definition: a piece of furniture with a mattress that people sleep on
senses.definitionCN: 供人睡觉的家具，上面铺有床垫
senses.example: The cat slept under the bed.
senses.why: Bed comes from a Germanic word for a sleeping place, and the furniture sense is the one children meet first.
senses.whyCN: bed 来自日耳曼语中表示「睡觉之处」的词，而「家具床」是孩子最先接触的意思。

senses.title: The bottom of a river or the sea
senses.definition: the ground beneath a river, lake or sea
senses.definitionCN: 河流、湖泊或海洋底部的地面
senses.example: The river bed was dry in summer.
senses.why: A river lies on its bed the way a sleeper lies on a bed, so the flat ground under water took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 河水躺在河床上，就像人躺在床里，于是水下那片平坦的地面也借用了 bed 这个名字。

senses.title: A plot of soil for plants
senses.definition: a piece of ground prepared for growing flowers or vegetables
senses.definitionCN: 整理好用来种花或种菜的土块
senses.example: She planted roses in the flower bed.
senses.why: A garden bed is a raised strip of prepared soil, shaped like a long low bed, which is why gardeners use the word.
senses.whyCN: 花坛是一条整理好、微微隆起的土畦，形状像一张长而低的床，园丁因此沿用 bed 这个词。

definition_en: a group of parents and children, all related people, or a group in biology
core_image: 晚饭桌边一家人围坐，老人、父母和孩子都在
scene: 晚饭桌边一家人围坐，老人、父母和孩子都在。 My family has five people.
sceneCN: 这里 family 是「家庭」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我家有五口人。

senses.title: Parents and children
senses.definition: parents and their children
senses.definitionCN: 父母与子女组成的一家
senses.example: My family has five people.
senses.why: Latin familia meant the whole household, including servants; English narrowed it to the parents and children who live together.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 familia 指包括仆人在内的整个家庭；英语把它收窄为一起生活的父母与子女。

senses.title: The whole clan
senses.definition: all the people related to one another
senses.example: The whole family came to the wedding.
senses.exampleCN: 全家族的人都来参加婚礼。
senses.why: The older household sense widened again to the whole line of relatives, so family can name a clan across generations.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的「家庭」义又扩展到所有亲属，因此 family 可以指跨世代的整个家族。

senses.title: The children of a couple
senses.definition: the children of a couple
senses.example: They want a large family.
senses.why: Because the children are the growing part of a household, family is often used for the children alone, as in a large family.
senses.whyCN: 因为孩子是家庭中不断增添的部分，family 常单独指孩子，如 a large family。

senses.title: A group in biology
senses.definition: a group of related plants or animals
senses.example: The cat belongs to the cat family.
senses.why: Biologists borrowed the word for a group of related species, keeping the picture of one household of living things.
senses.whyCN: 生物学家借这个词指一群亲缘相近的物种，保留了「同一家」的画面。

definition_zh: 大的；重要的；年长的；慷慨的
definition_en: large in size, importance or degree
core_image: 一只手掌张开，比划出抱不住那么大的一团
scene: 搬家的卡车停在巷口，纸箱堆得比门还高。 They moved the big table into the hall.
sceneCN: 这里 big 是「体积大」（第 01 个义项）；句意是一个大箱子堵住了门。

pos.zh: 形容词：大的、重要的、年长的

derivatives.zh: 由 big 加比较级后缀 -er 构成，义为「更大的」
由 big 加最高级后缀 -est 构成，义为「最大的」
由 big 加 -ness 构成，义为「巨大」

senses.title: Large in size
senses.definition: large in size or amount
senses.example: The box is too big for the shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 这个箱子太大，放不进架子。
senses.why: Big is a native word whose oldest meaning is simply large in size, and that physical sense remains the clearest one.
senses.whyCN: big 是本族词，最早的意思就是体积大，这个物理意义至今最清楚。

senses.title: Important or serious
senses.definition: important or serious in effect
senses.example: Learning to swim was a big step for him.
senses.exampleCN: 学会游泳对他来说是重要的一步。
senses.why: Something physically large takes more space and attention, so big easily shifts from size to importance.
senses.whyCN: 体积大的东西占据更多空间、也更受注意，所以 big 很容易从「尺寸」转向「重要性」。

senses.title: Older, of a sibling
senses.definition: older, used of a brother or sister
senses.definitionCN: 用于兄弟姐妹时表示年龄更大
senses.example: My big brother taught me to ride a bike.
senses.why: Children judge age by height and size, so the older sibling is naturally the big one in family speech.
senses.whyCN: 孩子常按身高和体型判断年龄，所以在家庭用语里，年长的兄弟姐妹自然就是 big 的那一个。

items.en: Big appears in northern English from about the fourteenth century; its origin is uncertain.
items.cn: big 约自十四世纪见于英格兰北部；来源不确定。

items.en: A link with a Scandinavian word for 'big, bulky' has been suggested but is not settled.
items.cn: 有人提出它与斯堪的纳维亚语中表示「大而笨重」的词有关，但未成定论。

items.en: The word spread south and replaced older terms for large size.

senses.title: The main meal of the day

senses.exampleCN: 他们七点坐下来吃晚饭。

senses.example: The school held a dinner for the new teachers.
senses.exampleCN: 学校为新老师办了一场晚宴。

branches.en: FOOD: a boiled egg on the plate.
BIRD: a hen sitting on her eggs.
SHAPE: an egg-shaped stone.
BIOLOGY: a frog's egg in the water.
CELL: one egg, one cell.
